svg.title: Figure 2 | Three acceptance scenarios for one claim
svg.desc: Each row identifies input conditions, expected behavior, and evidence to retain. A → B → C can be replayed on one claim, but no causal arrows connect rows. These are teaching scenarios, with no claim of current execution results.

g.font-family: Arial, Noto Sans CJK TC, sans-serif
g.text: Figure 2 | Three acceptance scenarios for one claim
Scenario A: incomplete data (negative test)
The applicant has no medical receipt. The system must identify the
missing required document and prevent staff from downloading a
report labeled complete.
Acceptance evidence: omission feedback, export-rejection test
results, and the actual interface.
Scenario B: complete all data (normal test)
Staff upload the receipt and validate again. The system marks
completion and allows JSON export; the report contents must be
correct.
Acceptance evidence: the actual export, field comparisons, and
passing execution records.
Scenario C: edit validated data (stale-result test)
Staff delete a previously entered medical-expense value. The system
must prevent downloading the earlier complete report and require
validation again.
Acceptance evidence: validation state after editing, invalidation
of the old download, and the repeated-validation operation record.
Each row identifies input conditions, expected behavior, and
evidence to retain. A → B → C can be replayed on one claim, but no
causal arrows connect rows. These are teaching scenarios, with no
claim of current execution results.
